stimulus.source_note: Theodor de Bry, engraving illustrating Bartolome de Las Casas, Narratio Regionum Indicarum, 1598, Smithsonian American Art Museum, CC0; the image is a European engraving made by an artist who never visited the Americas.
stimulus.text: The engraving, made by Theodor de Bry in 1598 to illustrate Bartolome de las Casas's account of Spanish actions in the Americas, shows Spanish soldiers torturing Indigenous people. A bound man lies over a fire in the foreground while soldiers stand around him, and more Indigenous people are held in a wooden structure behind. A handwritten French caption below calls them 'tortures to which the Indians are condemned.' Las Casas wrote his account to persuade the Spanish crown to stop the cruelty and reform the encomienda.

parts.prompt: Identify one thing the engraving shows about Spanish treatment of Indigenous peoples.
Explain one reason Las Casas's account, which this engraving illustrates, was written.
Explain one limitation of using this engraving as evidence about Spanish actions.

instruction: Answer each part in your own words from the stimulus only. Do not open the question file.
